acceptance_criteria: AC-1 (real bug, found live during AC-5 demonstration 1, relay/NXS-LOCAL-0012): a freshly-dispatched engineer session (orchestrator start, first spawn) can read/write the canonical relay file outside its own worktree (via NEXUS_CANONICAL_RELAY_DIR, section 3.6) -- confirmed, it posted RELAY_ACK and RELAY_QUESTION successfully. A RESUMED session (orchestrator start again, --resume <session_id> path, section 3.7) cannot -- its own report: 'Read attempt was auto-denied... this session has no approval surface, so any access outside the worktree is denied for the rest of the session, no retries possible.' This blocks every future recovery scenario where the resumed session needs to read a Product Owner decision posted to the canonical relay after the original process exited -- exactly the scenario section 3.7's own recovery design exists for.

AC-2: root-cause the actual mechanism before fixing -- verify for real (do not assume) whether this is (a) the engineer permission profile (.claude/nexus-engineer.settings.json) lacking an explicit additionalDirectories/equivalent grant for the canonical relay directory, so a fresh session's first access to that path happens to get an implicit allow that a --resume session's permission state does not carry forward, (b) a --resume-specific behavior of claude -p unrelated to this repo's own settings, or (c) something else -- name the confirmed mechanism in your SESSION_CLOSE evidence, not a guess.

AC-3: the fix makes resumed-session canonical-relay access as reliable as a fresh session's -- if AC-2 finds (a), add the canonical relay directory to the engineer profile's permissions.additionalDirectories (or the correct equivalent field) explicitly, so access does not depend on implicit fresh-session behavior at all, for either a fresh dispatch or a resume.

AC-4: a real, reproducible test: dispatch a throwaway scratch movement, let its engineer session post a RELAY_QUESTION and exit (matching NXS-LOCAL-0012's real shape), post a RELAY_DECISION on its relay file, then call orchestrator start again for the same movement and confirm the resumed session can actually read that RELAY_DECISION and proceed -- this is the literal scenario that failed live; reproduce it as your acceptance test, do not test a simplified proxy.
AC-5: no regression to fresh-dispatch access (already working) -- a fresh dispatch's relay read/write must keep working exactly as it does today.

AC-6: validation and state: the AC-4 reproduction is the primary evidence (a real dispatch+resume cycle, not merely a unit test of the settings file); any unit-level test on the permission-profile shape is additional, not a replacement. Project-state bookkeeping in this PR, including recording that this fix closes the finding from relay/NXS-LOCAL-0012's SESSION_CLOSE.

entries.subject: Fix committed locally; root-cause + AC-4 repro both real and confirmed; PR/merge/project-state still pending
entries.text: Root cause (AC-2), verified LIVE and directly in this very session (not assumed): with --permission-prompts none, a Read/Edit/Write-tool call needing approval outside the worktree has no approval surface, is auto-denied, and stays denied for the rest of the session with no retries -- this exact behavior hit my own Write/Edit tool calls repeatedly in this session. A fresh dispatch only ever appeared to work because it happened to route through Bash-invoked scripts/local_relay.py, which this per-tool directory allowlist does not gate; nothing guarantees a resumed session routes the same way. Fix (AC-3): scripts/orchestrator.py::_spawn_engineer now passes --add-dir <canonical_relay_dir> identically for dispatch and resume (commit 24ee588 on this branch); the static .claude/nexus-engineer.settings.json documents why the grant is a CLI flag, not a permissions.additionalDirectories entry (the canonical path is per-checkout, not something a committed file can hold). AC-4 real reproduction: dispatched a throwaway scratch movement (relay/NXS-LOCAL-0017, now CLOSED) through the real orchestrator -- fresh dispatch posted RELAY_ACK+RELAY_QUESTION and exited; I posted a RELAY_DECISION; a real orchestrator resume (pid 72588, no simplified proxy) re-read the canonical relay file fresh from disk and quoted the RELAY_DECISION's subject verbatim in its own RELAY_NOTE, closing the exact gap found live in relay/NXS-LOCAL-0012. AC-5: fresh dispatch was exercised in the same real run and still works. Also discovered in passing (documented, NOT fixed here -- out of this movement's scope per its own 'no other orchestrator.py behavior change' invariant): orchestrator.py never persists the real claude session_id (always None), so its 'resume' path never actually passes --resume to claude; it currently works only because a fresh re-spawn into the same worktree/branch behaves equivalently for this task shape. Flagging as a follow-up finding, not silently working around it. Unit tests added (tests/test_orchestrator.py, 2 new, both green) assert --add-dir is present identically for dispatch and resume. Targeted suite green: tests/test_orchestrator.py + test_local_relay_protocol.py + test_gov_po_role.py, 247 passed. STILL PENDING due to this session's own budget running out: full one-shot suite, project-state bookkeeping (project/build_history.json entry closing relay/NXS-LOCAL-0012's finding), push+PR+self-merge, and a formal SESSION_CLOSE packet. Reporting honestly rather than claiming completion -- a follow-up session should finish these before this branch is considered done.
